messages:
anika: onboarding marble11b (int4) canary started. seeing intermittent OOMs on dense-qa workload when prefetch is on. tagging infra + eng-ml for visibility.

ron: which host / instance type? and is this on dedicated canary or hosted?

anika: dedicated canary pool (p4d-ish). reproduces ~1/10 requests. stack shows allocation failure during KV prefetch: 
```
ERROR OutOfMemory: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
kv_prefetch: queued 48 entries, attempted 130MB reserve, failed at alloc 512MB
trace: slot_compactor triggered, free_slots=12, reserved=64MB
```

lucas: hmm. what are batch/max_new_tokens defaults for that rollout? prefetch + large max_new_tokens often amplifies transient spikes.

anika: rollout used defaults: batch_size=4, max_new_tokens=128, prefetch=true, kv_hot_threshold=0.6

mai: try two quick things: 1) lower max_new_tokens default to 64 for marble11b on canary; 2) enable `kv_walk` heuristic to trim cold keys instead of eager full-prefetch. both are non-disruptive. command: `redwoodctl config set marble11b --default.max_new_tokens=64`

lucas: +1. also try `--batch_size=1` for the canary to see if it's memory-pressure related. if OOMs stop, we know it's per-request allocation growth vs steady working set.

anika: rolling patch: set max_new_tokens=64 and batch_size=1 for canary; will keep prefetch=true initially to measure tail latency impact.

dev-bot: [alert] canary marble11b v0.3.1 failure-rate=4% (baseline 0.3%). recent deploy at 6567890100 rolled back automatically to v0.3.0 for high failure rate.

anika: confirmed rollback triggered by rollout controller. logs after rollback show reduced OOMs but still 1 spike in 500 requests. suspect compaction timing + slab fragmentation on the int4 allocator.

ron: can you dump allocator stats when spike happens? `redwoodctl debug heap-stats --model marble11b --node <id>` should show slab occupancy and freelist depth. paste sample when next spike occurs.

anika: pasting sample (sanitized):
```
heap_total: 24GB
skipped_free_chunks: 12
slab_sizes: [64MB: 120, 128MB: 48, 256MB: 12]
freelist_count: 8
avg_alloc_latency_ms: 1.8
compaction_runs_last_min: 0
```

mai: compaction_runs_last_min=0 is interesting. compactor should run on high fragmentation. is the compactor disabled for this canary? check feature flags `allocator.compactor.enabled` per pool.

anika: allocator.compactor.enabled = true. looks like compactor didn't trigger because `frag_threshold` default is 0.8 and measured frag ~0.76. close but below threshold.

lucas: two levers: 1) lower frag_threshold for canary to 0.7 so compaction triggers earlier; 2) enable a micro-defrag before prefetch: `allocator.defrag.pre_fetch=true`. both are safe for canary.

anika: applying patch: `redwoodctl feature set --pool canary-marble --allocator.frag_threshold=0.7` and `redwoodctl config set marble11b --allocator.defrag_pre_fetch=true`

anika: after patch: ran 10k requests, 0 OOMs, p95 latency +18ms with defrag prefetch on. will iterate: if latency regression >25ms we'll switch to prefetch=false and rely on streaming.

ron: nice. can we add an auto-fallback SLO rule: if failure_rate > 1% or p95_latency_increase > 25ms for 5m, automatically disable prefetch for that model/pool? reduces blast radius.

mai: yep, create rollout policy:
```
policy {
  trigger: failure_rate > 0.01 OR p95_latency_delta > 25ms FOR 5m
  action: set model.config.prefetch=false
}
```

anika: created policy and attached to canary-marble. will monitor next 24h and propose defaults for marble11b onboarding (batch=1, max_new_tokens=64, frag_threshold=0.7, defrag_pre_fetch=true).

lucas: let's also add a quality eval job to ensure lowering max_new_tokens doesn't regress dense-qa accuracy. schedule eval against nightly harness.

anika: scheduled eval run; initial diff looks within noise (<0.2% EM change). will post detailed eval when complete. thanks all :rocket:

mai: thanks — great triage. :thumbsup:

dev-bot: [info] eval job queued: eval-id=eval-6567890200
